clue.text: Greed spoils a victory

indicators.note: to spoil something is to ruin its shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Avarice ruins what should have been a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' tells you to rearrange A VICTORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Voracity is ravenous, insatiable appetite, a close synonym of greed.

clue.text: Academic stream producing double firsts.

parts.note: a river flowing through a university city, whose students take top degrees in two subjects

explanation.surface: A university river that turns out students with top honours twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name of the Thames as it runs through Oxford, a university that awards 'double firsts' (first-class honours in two exams).
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of the Thames at Oxford goes by this name, so it is the stream of a seat of learning.

clue.text: A nonentity, he enters Mediterranean island without us

indicators.note: one piece entering another means it goes inside it
without means the named letters are left out of the island's name

parts.note: Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man of no importance arrives on a Mediterranean island, leaving the rest of us behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without us' removes US from CYPRUS, leaving CYPR; 'enters' puts HE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cypher is a person of no importance, a mere zero or figurehead.

clue.text: Get husband to stay like that

indicators.note: the letters stay put inside the run of clue words, waiting to be read off

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep their husband from leaving, just like that.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'geT HUSband'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus means in this way, so it stands for 'like that'.

clue.text: Taking steps to change the monarch

indicators.note: changing the words here means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A revolutionary plan to replace the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' asks you to rearrange THE MONARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An army on the march is advancing step by step, so the phrase means marching or taking steps.

clue.text: Run up feature about a cause

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: about means going round the next piece
in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature
taken as written

explanation.surface: A manager tallies a run of results while mulling over a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NOSE into ESON, and 'about' wraps it round A to give EASON, which follows R.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is the grounds or motive behind something, its cause.

clue.text: Menial trails after main group

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail after them
the body of something is its main part or group

explanation.surface: A lowly servant tags along behind the main party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like it tells you to put one piece behind the other, but it belongs to the phrase 'trails after', which means DOGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is a drudge given all the menial jobs.

clue.text: Deliberate new problem initially found in our attitude

indicators.note: found in means these letters are placed inside the next word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of problem

parts.note: a pose is an attitude or stance someone strikes

explanation.surface: A fresh difficulty seems to arise from our own deliberate stance.
explanation.walkthrough: N and the first letter of 'problem' go inside OUR to give ONPUR, then POSE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on purpose means doing it intentionally, which is what deliberate means.

clue.text: Watch one going to meet horse

definitions.meaning: a pocket watch with a hinged cover over its face
someone who rides to a meet, the gathering of a fox hunt
a strong horse bred for riding to hounds

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the rider setting off to meet a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'meet' is the gathering of riders and hounds before a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a type of hinged pocket watch, a person who hunts, and a breed of riding horse used for hunting.

clue.text: Put question to a retiring author

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: to pose a question is to put it to someone

explanation.surface: Someone tries to interview a shy writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses POSE A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek writer credited with the famous fables.

clue.text: Repeatedly very hard to keep American secret

indicators.note: repeatedly means the piece is used twice over
to keep means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: HH is the pencil-lead grade for very hard

explanation.surface: It is extremely difficult to keep an American's secret again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: HH (the very-hard pencil grade) holds US to make one half; 'Repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hush-hush is kept highly confidential, that is, secret.

clue.text: Treat for children from red-haired baker

parts.note: ginger describes reddish hair
a baker is a man who makes bread

explanation.surface: A red-headed baker makes a treat for the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingerbread man is a figure-shaped biscuit that is a favourite treat for youngsters.

clue.text: The oldest branch of medicine

parts.note: not the most ancient field of healing but the field devoted to treating the elderly

explanation.surface: A claim about which medical specialty came first in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oldest' suggests the earliest in history; it means the medical field for the oldest patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatric medicine is the specialty concerned with the care of elderly people.

clue.text: Wearing a thin fabric, Pat may be shunned

indicators.note: Pat wearing a fabric means the fabric goes around Pat

parts.note: voile is a thin, semi-transparent fabric
to dab is to pat lightly

explanation.surface: Someone called Pat, dressed in flimsy cloth, might find people steering clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a person's name but is the verb DAB, placed inside VOILE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be shunned is something that can be avoided.

clue.text: Care about protecting a plant

indicators.note: protecting means the outer piece shields the next piece inside it
about here means turned around, read backwards

parts.note: care in the sense of anxiety is worry

explanation.surface: A gardener tends a plant and shields it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses WORRY to YRROW, and 'protecting' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a common wild flower with feathery leaves and flat white flower heads.

clue.text: Iris following male in dance

parts.note: orris is a kind of iris whose root is used in perfume

explanation.surface: A woman called Iris follows her partner across the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts ORRIS after M. 'Iris' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris is a traditional English folk dance performed with bells and sticks.

clue.text: Subtle marketing-loss felt badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together in a poor, jumbled order

explanation.surface: A gentle sales approach leads to losses that are keenly felt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' asks you to rearrange LOSS FELT.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft sell is a low-pressure, persuasive style of advertising or selling.

clue.text: Burke and Hare's spell of night work?

definitions.text: Burke and Hare's spell of night work?

parts.words: Burke and Hare's spell of night work?
parts.note: the after-dark labours of two famous corpse suppliers, read as a stint of work through the night

explanation.surface: A question about when two notorious criminals did their work.
explanation.walkthrough: Burke and Hare were notorious 1820s Edinburgh murderers who sold bodies to anatomists, and body-snatchers dug corpses out of cemeteries at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The graveyard shift is the overnight work period, typically midnight to morning.

clue.text: Kitchen utensil sounds more important

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Kitchen utensil sounds more important' (no count), gives GRATER (sounds like GREATER), not the printed answer GRATE; the clue appears cut or misread

clue.text: Girl's double dropping head in book

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name; the 's reads as 'has'

indicators.note: dropping its head means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: dual means double

explanation.surface: A girl's twin loses their head over a book.
explanation.walkthrough: DUAL without its first letter is UAL, which follows ANN.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book published once a year, such as a children's yearly gift volume.

clue.text: Scold one chap loudly — and wrongly

indicators.note: loudly means the piece is spoken out, so its sound matters, not its spelling

parts.note: Harry is one man's name

indicators.note: wrongly means the word's letters are set in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A man shouts at someone, and unfairly so.
explanation.walkthrough: HARRI is said like Harry; 'wrongly' rearranges AND into DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, nagging old woman, a scold in the old sense of a shrew.

clue.text: Double act that's now defunct

indicators.note: double means the piece appears twice

parts.note: to do is to act or perform

explanation.surface: A comedy duo whose double act has died a death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double act' reads as a comedy pair, but means DO twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct flightless bird of Mauritius is the byword for something long gone.

clue.text: University in fens is not what it seems

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: fens are marshes or bogs

explanation.surface: A university in the Fens turns out to be a sham.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low marshland around Cambridge, which makes the surface's university plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bogus is fake, a sham that looks genuine but is not.

clue.text: Happy? Good boy!

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Praising a dog: a happy good boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad is a plain synonym for pleased or happy.

clue.text: Securely protected, used a weapon and traded illegally

definitions.meaning: enclosed by a barrier round the edge

explanation.surface: A villain locks up safely, wields a sword and deals in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers enclosing land with a barrier, sword-fighting in sport, and handling stolen goods for resale.

clue.text: People go into a fit subject

indicators.note: go into means these letters enter the space between the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
fit in the sense of capable is able
men are people

explanation.surface: People get into a state of suitability for a topic.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN goes between A and ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable means liable or answerable, as in 'subject to' a law.
